Independent native Praat LPC reference

Captured from Praat 7.0.03beta (October 13 2026) on macOS. The compressed JSON
records the native executable SHA-256, source speech hash, exact float32 PCM
and hashes, native LPC coefficients/gain, full Spectrum response and frame time.
No expected values are calculated by the WASM adapter or its JS helpers.

Six inputs cover speech, a four-resonance synthetic vowel and noise, 24/44.1/48
kHz capture rates, 5/5.5/6 kHz ceilings, orders 10/14, pre-emphasis 0/50/100 Hz
and effective Gaussian windows 15/25/40 ms. Inputs use float32 WAV to preserve
exact equality between native and WASM samples. Synthetic input generation is
seeded; speech is from the unchanged public-domain LibriVox regression fixture.

Native commands: Resample (precision 50), To LPC (burg), To Spectrum (slice)
with bandwidth reduction 0 and de-emphasis disabled. One centered frame is
requested using a one-second frame step. Native coefficients use denominator
signs; API coefficients use the opposite, positive predictor signs. The gain
is converted from native summed error to mean error by dividing by frame size.
Native Spectrum squared magnitude is multiplied by analysisRate*df/frameSize
to remove its FFT scaling. Tests compare every envelope bin, not only peaks.

The fixture hash in lpc-native.json is verified before use. Builds never run
capture or rewrite references. To explicitly recapture using an independently
built native executable:

python3 scripts/capture-lpc-reference.py --praat /absolute/path/to/Praat --output tests/fixtures/lpc-native.json.gz

Review the source, version, cases and numerical differences, then update the
metadata hash explicitly. Do not regenerate fixtures to make a failing test pass.
Current guards: coefficient absolute error <1e-6, relative mean gain error <1e-8,
and maximum full-envelope dB error <1e-4. Mutations of coefficients, gain, a
non-peak bin and actual pre-emphasis settings must be rejected by these guards.
